summary: Shoko Watanabe was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji and under Ernst Leumann, later receiving a doctorate from Toyo University. His posts included Taisho, Kyushu, and Toyo universities.

Shoku Bando is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University of Education, Otani University, and the University of Freiburg. In 1987, he was affiliated with Fukui Prefectural College, Kyoto University, and the Abhidharma Institute.

Shoryu Katsura works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University and earned his Ph.D. at the University of Toronto under Anthony Kennedy Warder. He held professorships at Hiroshima University (1976–2004) and Ryukoku University (2004–2015).

Shoshin Fukihara was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Horyuji Kangakuin and Otani University under Susumu Yamaguchi and Join Saeki. He held posts at Otani University, Otani University Junior College, Doho University, and Otani Senshu Gakuin.

Shoshin Ichishima is a Buddhist studies scholar. He served as a visiting lecturer in Tibetan Buddhism at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa and held several posts at Taisho University, where he became Professor Emeritus (attested 2014).

Shoshin Kuwayama is a scholar of history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University (~1957–1966) and served there from ~1966 to 2002, becoming Professor Emeritus at the Institute for Research in the Humanities.

Shoshun Hayashidera is a scholar in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. Affiliated with the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies in 2011, Hayashidera's career includes an appointment as Professor at Hokkaido University (attested 2026).

Shoson Miyamoto was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University, the University of Tokyo, and the University of Oxford (Ph.D.). He held professorships at the University of Tokyo, Waseda University, and Komazawa University.

Shou-chien Shih is a scholar of sinology and history/archaeology. A doctoral student at National Sun Yat-sen University, he served as a professor at National Taiwan University (~1984–1997) and as director of the National Palace Museum (~2004–2006).

Shozen Kumoi was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Otani University and under Erich Frauwallner at the University of Vienna. He taught at Otani University (1948–1981; later emeritus) and Bukkyo University (1982).

Shri Krishna Saksena was a scholar in the fields of philosophy and Indology. During his academic career, he held posts as Professor at the University of Lucknow and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa.
Shri Krishna Sharma was an Indology and linguistics scholar. Beyond his academic work, which included teaching Dieter Schuh, he founded the Hindu Maha Sabha and DAV College, Suva.

Shridhar Ramakrishna Bhandarkar was an Indologist. He served as Assistant to the Professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College (1884), Professor of Sanskrit at Elphinstone College (~1884–1915), and permanent Professor of Sanskrit at Wilson College, Mumbai.

Shridhar Tryambak Pathak was an Indologist. His career posts included serving as a Shastri at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 1921) and as a Sanskrit Teacher at Elphinstone College (attested 1927).

Shrikant S. Bahulkar works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Vasudev Vishwanath Gokhale, was a professor at Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth (1981–2009), served as Chief Editor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, and was affiliated with BORI (2021).

Sri Narayana Mishra was a scholar in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy who studied under Anantalal Thakur. He spent his career at Banaras Hindu University, serving as Lecturer (1971), Reader (1985), and eventually Professor Emeritus of Sanskrit (attested 2010).

Shripad Krishna Belvalkar was an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Kashinath Bapu Pathak and Charles Rockwell Lanman. He was Professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College (~1914–1927) and served as Secretary and General Editor of the Mahabharata at BORI.

Shrivatsa Goswami is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who studied at Banaras Hindu University. He taught philosophy and religion at Banaras Hindu University, was a visiting scholar at Harvard University, and was affiliated with Vrindaban Research Institute.

Shu-chen Chen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. She earned her PhD at the University of Virginia, where she also worked as a teaching assistant (1996), studying under doctoral supervisors Jeffrey Hopkins and Karen Christina Lang.

Shu-fen Chen is a scholar in linguistics and Indology. She studied at National Tsing Hua University under Chin-Fa Lien and completed doctoral work under Hans Henrich Hock, later serving as a professor at National Tsing Hua University (attested 2010).
